MAJOR: `architect_review_check.py` except clause references `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, but the diff shows no `import subprocess` being added to that module. If it is not already imported, the handler raises `NameError` at the exact moment a git failure occurs (the test `test_check_fails_closed_when_git_missing` would be the canary). Must be verified against the actual file — a fail-closed path that crashes with the wrong exception type undermines the whole point of the change.

Behavior change is fail-closed but not audited at all call sites: `precheck._git()` previously returned `""` on any failure; it now raises `GitError` for a non-zero exit. Only `_changed_files()` is wrapped. Any other `_git(...)` caller in `precheck.py` (e.g. `git status`, `git ls-files` for untracked discovery, `rev-parse`) that relied on the empty-string contract will now abort precheck with a hard failure. Same concern for `architect_review.py`: only the three call sites shown were converted; any remaining `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` in that file still decodes with the OS locale, silently reintroducing the exact bug being fixed.

`_integration_ref()` + `SystemExit` makes precheck fatal when neither `develop` nor `origin/develop` resolves. In shallow CI checkouts (`fetch-depth: 1`, PR-only ref) `merge-base`/`rev-parse` on `develop` fails, so a pipeline that previously degraded to "no changed files" now hard-fails. Fail-closed is the right policy, but the shallow-clone CI path must be demonstrated to still pass before this ships.

Module-identity split in the test suite: `from scripts.dev import architect_review as ar` was replaced with `sys.path.insert(scripts/dev)` + `import architect_review as ar`. `architect_review` and `scripts.dev.architect_review` now exist as two distinct module objects in the same pytest session. Any other test (or `gate1_check`, which likely imports via the package path) monkeypatching `scripts.dev.architect_review.ROOT` will not affect `ar.ROOT` here and vice versa — flaky, order-dependent test behavior that will get worse as tests grow.
MINOR: AC third bullet claims "the duplicate CI-sha evidence workaround is no longer needed", but the diff contains no removal of any workaround artifact/baseline entry. Either it was missed or the AC is only partially satisfied; evidence of removal should be in the change set.
`architect_review_check.py` wraps only `changed_files()`/`diff_sha()`; `_baseline_shas()` and later git-touching logic (if any) remain outside the handler, leaving a partial fail-closed boundary.

`git_text` now applies a 30s default timeout to `precheck._git`, which previously had none. On a large monorepo `git diff --name-only` of a wide range could exceed it and turn a working precheck into a fatal timeout; the timeout should be explicit/parameterizable per call site rather than a single global default.

The `"\ufffd" in out` warning fires whenever the diff legitimately contains U+FFFD (e.g. reviewing a file with replacement chars), producing false-positive stderr noise in CI logs — a warning channel that cries wolf weakens observability.

`gitutil.git_text` is imported into `architect_review.py` under a `_git_text_shared` alias and re-exported through a local `_git_text` wrapper while `precheck.py` wraps it as `_git`; three names for one policy reduces greppability. A single documented entry point (or none) would be cleaner.
NIT: `gitutil.py` warning line prints argv with `join` (no `repr`), inconsistent with the `GitError` messages that do use `repr` — cosmetic inconsistency in log formatting.
Test file gains a trailing blank line and mixes `sys.path` mutation with relative module imports; standard pattern is a `conftest.py` path fixture rather than per-file `sys.path.insert` duplication.
`documentation-index.html` regenerated without a trailing newline (pre-existing, but regenerated here so it perpetuates).

Language rule check: `gitutil.py` is new shipped Python — acceptable because it lives under `scripts/dev` (tooling carve-out), but this should be stated explicitly in the PR description so the Go-first standard is visibly honored rather than implicitly assumed.
SUMMARY: Sound direction: a single shared UTF-8/fail-closed git helper with a real regression test is the right fix for a locale-dependent review sha, and fail-closed on broken git is correct policy.

Top risks: the unverified `subprocess` import in `architect_review_check.py`, unaudited remaining `text=True`/empty-string git call sites in both `architect_review.py` and `precheck.py`, and the new hard-failure path on shallow CI checkouts where `develop` refs are absent.

Secondary: test-module identity split (`architect_review` vs `scripts.dev.architect_review`) and the AC's unfulfilled "remove the CI-sha workaround" claim. Recommend merge only after those three verifications are shown green on both Windows and CI.
